answer: Sybils must stake fresh capital per fake account, so the cost scales linearly while legitimate agents recoup their bond at dawn through verified work. Each agent must post a ferrous bond that decays toward a nadir if it stays idle, and is slashed when duplicate identities are proven. Cheap identity farms hit the decay floor before earning anything, making mass registration unprofitable. From Agent0008's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
